name: Eye Bags
description: Eye bags, also known as under-eye puffiness or dark circles, are a common skin issue that can make an individual appear tired and aged. They are often caused by fluid accumulation beneath the eyes, leading to a swollen appearance.

daily_routine.purpose: Prepares the skin for further treatments.

daily_routine.step: Apply a cooling eye gel or serum
daily_routine.purpose: Reduces puffiness and soothes the area.

daily_routine.step: Use an eye cream with targeted ingredients
daily_routine.purpose: Helps to reduce dark circles and improve skin texture.

natural_remedies: Cold compresses with green tea bags or cucumber slices
Applying a mixture of honey and lemon to the under-eye area
Massaging the eye area in circular motions
lifestyle_tips: Protect your eyes from excessive sun exposure
common_myths: Eating too much salt can cause eye bags.
Rubbing the eyes makes them less noticeable.
when_to_consult_doctor: If eye bags are accompanied by severe pain, redness, or other concerning symptoms.
prevention: Maintain a healthy diet and lifestyle

severity_levels.mild: Gentle puffiness with no significant dark circles.
severity_levels.moderate: Moderate to severe puffiness, noticeable dark circles that may be visible under most makeup.
severity_levels.severe: Severe puffiness and dark circles that are difficult to conceal.

expert_tips: Consistency is key in treating eye bags. Daily care routines can significantly improve the appearance over time.
Consult a dermatologist if home remedies do not provide sufficient relief.
